plan.summary: This first 4-week block is a simple off-camp build for a beginner boxer with only 1 S&C session per week and higher sparring priorities. Week 1 establishes training maxes for the primary lower-body lift so percentage work can start cleanly, and the main training weeks begin in Week 2. The block emphasizes safe power first, then foundational strength, then a small amount of upper-body pulling, trunk work, and brief conditioning without adding unnecessary fatigue to boxing practice.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build safe foundational strength and general power while keeping soreness and fatigue low enough for sparring.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the main force qualities with slightly heavier work while keeping power crisp and recoverable.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Shift more of the work toward faster explosive output while holding onto the strength built earlier.

exercises.name: 1a. Box Jump
exercises.notes: Use a box height you can land on quietly and confidently. Reset between reps and keep each jump fast and crisp.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if box setup is awkward. Stick the landing and reset each rep.

substitutionOptions.name: Trap Bar Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only with very light load and clean technique. Keep every rep snappy.

exercises.name: 2. Back Squat
exercises.notes: Brace hard, keep depth consistent, and stop if form breaks. This session sets your baseline for future percentage-based work.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to one hard set of 3-5 reps with solid form. Log the load and reps so the app can estimate your training max.

substitutionOptions.name: Safety Bar Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if available and more comfortable on the shoulders.

substitutionOptions.name: Goblet Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if barbell squatting is not yet safe or comfortable. Push the load as high as good form allows for the top set.

exercises.name: 3. Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.notes: Control the lowering phase, pause briefly at the bottom, and press smoothly without bouncing. Leave 2 reps in reserve.

substitutionOptions.name: Barbell Bench Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you have a reliable spotter and stable technique.

substitutionOptions.name: Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if pressing strength is still building or benches are busy.

exercises.name: 4. Chest-Supported Row
exercises.notes: Pull the elbows back hard and control the return. Keep the chest planted and avoid shrugging.

substitutionOptions.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if no chest-supported bench is free. Keep the torso stable.

substitutionOptions.name: Seated Cable Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you want a simpler setup and smoother resistance.

exercises.name: 5. Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.notes: Keep ribs down and glutes tight. Only roll out as far as you can without losing trunk position.

substitutionOptions.name: Barbell Rollout
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if no ab wheel is available.

substitutionOptions.name: Cable Crunch
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if rollouts irritate the lower back.

exercises.name: 6. Air Bike Intervals
exercises.notes: Keep the pace hard but repeatable and finish fresher than a boxing conditioning day.
